subject: Integration playbook: SDK auth, routing, embeddings & safe prompt policy
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novana.health>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration playbook: SDK auth, routing, embeddings & safe prompt policy

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap of what we agreed and suggested next steps so we can lock timelines from your side: 

1) SDK + Auth
- We recommended using the Redwood SDK for server-side calls and short-lived signed tokens for browser flows. Dev will attach a 10-minute quickstart doc.
- Action: Novana to confirm whether they'll use a proxy service (preferred) or integrate direct client SDKs.

2) Routing & model variants
- We proposed latency-first routing in us-west for patient-facing flows and cost-tier fallback (quantized variant) for batch jobs.
- Action: please share your expected qps and percent of interactive traffic.

3) Embeddings / Reranker
- We suggested separate embedding pipeline for indexing EHR metadata + a small reranker model for relevance filtering. We can provide an autoscaling recipe.

4) Prompt governance & safety
- High-level: prompt templates should be versioned in a single repo with an immutable digest (we shared a sample YAML). Red-team window and prompt-injection mitigations (input sanitation and output validators) are recommended.
- Action: Novana to share existing prompt templates or a small corpus for a red-team exercise.

Next steps / timings:
- Dev will send the SDK quickstart + an auth sample by EOD Monday (attached as PDF).
- Schedule a 60-min technical workshop next week (Dev + Novana engineers) to walk through token flows, routing policy, and embedding ops.
- We can also run a 1-day red-team session following the workshop to stress-test prompt templates.

If that matches your expectation I’ll send calendar invites for workshop slots on Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Jonas — this is great, thanks. Couple clarifying questions before we lock the workshop time: 

- For client-side interactions (patient chat widget) we need to avoid leaking PHI. You mentioned short-lived signed tokens — can you confirm SDK supports token rotation and scoping? Any sample for server-side signing flow?

- For embeddings pipeline: we currently store EHR snippets in a managed DB with strict access controls. Will the embedding step require copying data outside our VPC, or can it run within our Private deployment?

- Prompt governance: we have a small catalog (20 templates) but no versioning. Will the red-team be able to run against a staging copy only? Also curious about automated checks you mentioned (prompt-injection and hallucination detectors) — are those in Redwood Optimize or custom rules we run?

Thanks — can Marissa or Dev propose Wed 10–11am or Thu 2–3pm ET for the workshop?

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product, Novana Health

Elena — quick technical replies inline: 

1) Token rotation / scoping
- Yes: Redwood SDK supports server-side signing and returning short-lived tokens with scope claims (models, TTL, allowed routes). Typical pattern: backend mints a token (10m) via signed JWT using your KMS; client uses token to call our edge endpoint.
- Attached: auth-sample.js and quickstart PDF with code snippets.

2) Private deployment for embeddings
- We can run embedding jobs inside your Private deployment (on-prem/VPC) — no data needs to leave your network. We'll ship a lightweight runner that writes vectors to your managed DB or an S3-compatible store in your VPC.

3) Prompt governance & red-team
- Redwood Optimize provides a rules engine for automated checks (prompt injection heuristics, forbidden token matchers, output schema validation). For audits and red-team runs we normally run against a staging project that mirrors prod prompts and data.
- For versioning we recommend a git-based prompts repo with enforced CI that lints templates, runs a suite of unit-evals, and tags releases (we included prompt_versioning_template.yaml as a starting point).

Proposed workshop agenda (60 min):
- 0–15m: auth/token flows + SDK quickstart walkthrough
- 15–35m: routing policies & model variant considerations (latency vs cost tiers)
- 35–50m: embedding pipeline topology + reranker tuning
- 50–60m: prompt governance primer & red-team plan

I can join Wed 10–11am ET (works for our engineering team). Sending calendar invite separately.

--
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
